judgments.reasoning_cat1: "shall not be unreasonably withheld" appears twice and "effectively associate" is an odd, undefined formulation, though the no-duty-to-defend rule itself is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Important Notice (c029) and the advancement provision (c096).
judgments.clause_name: Section IX.A - No Duty to Defend

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Advancement duty with a repayment obligation and an "established" trigger; reasonably precise.

judgments.clause_name: Section IX.B - Advancement of Defense Costs

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "as soon as practicable" coupled with an outside 60-day limit creates the standard tension between the two standards, and the notice duty is cast as a condition precedent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: For Discovery Period claims, the 60-day outside limit can extend beyond the Discovery Period itself, and Section X(B) requires circumstance notice within the Policy Period, so the timing rules must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "circumstances which may give rise to a Claim" is inherently vague, while the second sentence imposes strict particularity as a condition precedent — the two pull against each other.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is reinforced by Section III's statement that circumstance notice cannot be given during the Discovery Period; consistent, if strict.
judgments.clause_name: Section X.B - Notice of Potential Claims

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short routing provision whose verb is lost to OCR but whose meaning is obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches Item 5 (c013) exactly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "all information reasonably requested" and "such ... assistance and cooperation as the Insurer may reasonably request" are evaluative but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section IX(A)(2)'s entitlement to full information; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The five triggers and three conditions precedent are specifically drafted; "any non-bank entity" in limb (1) is broad but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This subsection is deleted and replaced by endorsement 2223 (c179) with a 20% rather than 25% threshold, and then deleted entirely by the Discovery Period endorsement (c006), so the operative text on the face of the document is inconsistent.
judgments.clause_name: Section XII.A - Mergers, acquisitions, changes requiring consent

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear automatic-coverage promise keyed to a numerical asset threshold.

judgments.clause_name: Section XII.B - Automatic coverage for small bank acquisitions

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "arising out of or directly or indirectly resulting from" any prior Wrongful Act is very broad, and the paragraph ends with a comma rather than a period, leaving the sentence formally incomplete.

judgments.clause_name: Section XII.C - No coverage for prior Wrongful Acts

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 90% rule and the multi-year proration rule sit uneasily: it is not clear whether 90% or prorata applies to a cancellation after the first anniversary of a multi-year policy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is a three-year policy that was extended by one month, so the anniversary mechanics matter, and Section XIII(C)(2) separately declares the premium fully earned on conversion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The notice periods and mailing provisions are precise, and "for any other reason" is a plain residual.

judgments.clause_name: Section XIII.B - Insurer Cancellation or Nonrenewal

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Trigger (c), "the Company ceasing to engage actively in its primary business", is vague, and "substantially all of the assets" adds a second imprecise boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection (2) preserves the Discovery Period right on any of these events, whereas Section III limits that right to conversion under (C)(1)(b) alone — a squarely inconsistent pair.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "based on the relative legal exposures of the parties" is an inherently indeterminate standard, though the 100% presumption in (1)(a) is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is coordinated with the arbitration mechanism in Section XIV(B) and the advancement duty; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "best efforts", "which the Insurer believes to be covered", and arbitration only "if requested by the Insured" make the mechanism one-sidedly optional, though the panel-selection rules are precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits with Section IX(B) advancement and Section XIV(A) allocation, and with Section XVI(F) on actions against the Insurer; no contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subparagraph (2) states the Policy "shall not be deemed to be a series of individual insurance contracts", which sits directly against (1)'s instruction that the Application be construed as a separate application by each Insured Person; the negative looks like a drafting error that reverses the usual severability formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That reading is difficult to reconcile with Section XV(B) and (C), which withhold coverage only from knowing individuals and disclaim imputation between Insured Persons — i.e. treat the contract as severable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing sentence, "whether or not the Insured Person actually knew if the misrepresentation or untruthful disclosure was made", is garbled and appears to contradict the knowledge requirement in limb (1).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with c109(2)'s statement that the Policy is not a series of individual contracts, and with the no-imputation rule in c111(1); the interlocking severability provisions do not read smoothly together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The rule is stated in two crisp limbs, expressly naming Exclusions (G) and (H) for imputation to the Company.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Naming only (G) and (H) invites an expressio unius reading against other exclusions, and it must be read with c109(2) and c110; some tension but manageable.
